+OOXML uses EMU (English Metric Units): 914400 EMU = 1 inch = 72 pt. Standard widescreen slides are 12192000 × 6858000 EMU (13.33" × 7.5").
+To position a shape **near the bottom and horizontally centered**:
+<!-- Near-bottom: y ≥ 85% of slide height (e.g., y=5829300 for a 6858000-tall slide) -->
+y = slide_height - shape_height - 457200  # near bottom with margin
+**Always read `ppt/presentation.xml` for actual slide dimensions** (`<p:sldSz cx="..." cy="..."/>`) — do not assume standard sizes.

+### Recovering missing values in existing spreadsheets

+When replacing `???` or `N/A` placeholders in an existing workbook, **write Excel formulas that derive the value from the surrounding data — do NOT compute the answer in Python and hardcode the result**.
+sheet['K5'] = 19285          # computed in Python; will break if other data changes
+# ✅ CORRECT — write an Excel formula that mirrors the relationship
+sheet['K5'] = '=SUM(B5:J5)'  # total = sum of all directorate budgets in that row
+1. Read each sheet to understand the patterns and cell relationships
+2. For each `???` cell, look at neighboring cells to determine the formula
+3. Write a formula string — never a Python-computed number
+4. Run `recalc.py` after saving to update all cached values
+5. Verify no formula errors remain (`status: "success"` in recalc.py output)

+**CRITICAL**: A pandas `groupby` or `pivot_table` call writes STATIC DATA to a sheet — it is NOT an Excel pivot table. If the task requires real Excel pivot tables (with rows/columns/aggregation you can drag in Excel), you must use openpyxl's pivot API. Tests that check pivot table configuration (row fields, aggregation type, cache fields) will fail if you write static data instead.
+### Required structure for a real Excel pivot table
+1. A **SourceData** sheet with the raw (unaggregated) data including ALL source columns
+2. A **CacheDefinition** that describes the source range and its fields
+3. A **PivotTable** definition attached to the output sheet, with `rowFields`, `dataFields`, and optionally `colFields`
+from openpyxl.pivot.table import PivotTable, PivotField, DataField, Location
+# 1. Build SourceData sheet with raw data
+for row in data_rows:   # list of tuples matching headers
+# 3. Build CacheDefinition — one CacheField per column in SourceData
+        CacheField(name=h, numFmtId=0) for h in headers
+# 4. Build PivotTable — field indices match position in headers list
+    dataFields=[DataField(name="Sum of EARNERS", fld=1, subtotal="sum")]  # sum EARNERS
+- `rowFields=[PivotField(x=N)]` — N is the 0-based index of the field in `headers`
+- `dataFields=[DataField(fld=N, subtotal="sum")]` — use `"sum"` for Sum, `"count"` for Count
+- `colFields=[PivotField(x=N)]` — add column fields the same way as row fields
+- Every column in the source data must have a corresponding `CacheField`
+- The `ref` in `WorksheetSource` must cover all data rows including the header row
+After saving, run `recalc.py` to populate the pivot cache values.
